learn: Spanish is a phonetic language: words are mostly pronounced as they are spelled.
The five vowels are always clear: a (ah), e (eh), i (ee), o (oh), u (oo).
Special sounds: ñ (as in "canyon"), rr (a rolled r), j (a breathy h), and a silent h.
lessons.try: Read ten Spanish words aloud, paying attention to vowels.

learn: Hola, buenos días, buenas tardes, buenas noches.
Adiós, hasta luego, hasta mañana, nos vemos.
Formal "usted" is for adults and strangers; "tú" is for friends and family.
lessons.try: Greet five people using the right formality.

learn: "¿Cómo te llamas?" / "Me llamo..." "¿Cómo se llama usted?" is the formal form.
"Te presento a..." means "Let me introduce you to..."
"Encantado" (male) or "encantada" (female) means "Delighted to meet you."
check: The formal way to ask a name is...
lessons.try: Introduce a friend to a teacher in Spanish.

learn: Review 0 to 100: cero, uno... veinte, treinta... cien.
Hundreds: doscientos (200), trescientos (300), quinientos (500), mil (1,000).
Combine: ciento cincuenta y dos (152).
lessons.try: Say the prices of five items in Spanish.

learn: Days: lunes to domingo. Months: enero to diciembre (not capitalised).
"Hoy es martes, el doce de octubre."
"El primero de mayo" is used for the first of the month.
lessons.try: Write the dates of five family birthdays.

learn: "¿Qué hora es?" "Es la una." "Son las dos y cuarto." (2:15) "Son las tres menos diez." (2:50)
"De la mañana" (a.m.), "de la tarde" (afternoon), "de la noche" (night).
Many Spanish-speaking countries use the 24-hour clock for schedules.
lessons.try: Write your daily schedule with times in Spanish.

learn: Every Spanish noun is masculine or feminine.
Most nouns ending in -o are masculine (el libro); most ending in -a are feminine (la mesa).
Exceptions exist: el día, la mano, el mapa.
lessons.try: Sort twenty nouns into masculine and feminine.

learn: Definite (the): el, la, los, las.
Indefinite (a, an, some): un, una, unos, unas.
Articles match the noun's gender and number.
lessons.try: Add the correct articles to ten nouns.

learn: El pupitre (desk), la pizarra (board), el bolígrafo (pen), la calculadora, el reloj (clock).
Classroom phrases: "¿Cómo se dice...?" (How do you say...?), "No entiendo" (I don't understand), "Repita, por favor."
"¿Puedo ir al baño?" (May I go to the bathroom?)
lessons.try: Label your workspace in Spanish.

learn: Ser: soy, eres, es, somos, sois (Spain, informal "you all"), son.
Use ser for identity, origin, profession and traits.
"Somos estudiantes" means "We are students."
lessons.try: Describe yourself with five sentences using ser.

learn: Alto/bajo (tall/short), rubio/moreno (blond/dark-haired), pelirrojo (red-haired), joven/mayor (young/old).
"Tiene el pelo largo" (has long hair). "Tiene los ojos azules" (has blue eyes).
Adjectives agree in gender and number.
lessons.try: Describe a famous person without naming them; others guess.

learn: Simpático (nice), antipático (unpleasant), trabajador (hardworking), perezoso (lazy), gracioso (funny), serio (serious).
Use "muy" (very), "bastante" (quite) and "un poco" (a little).
"No es nada perezoso" means "He's not at all lazy."
lessons.try: Write a description of your best friend's personality.

learn: Remove -ar and add: -o, -as, -a, -amos, -áis, -an.
Hablar: hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, habláis, hablan.
The present tense means "I speak", "I am speaking" or "I do speak".
lessons.try: Conjugate trabajar, estudiar and tomar.

learn: Bailar, cantar, nadar, escuchar, mirar, llegar, comprar, cocinar, tocar (play an instrument), usar.
"Toco la guitarra" means "I play the guitar."
"Miro la televisión" means "I watch television."
lessons.try: Write ten sentences with different -ar verbs.

learn: Question words: ¿qué? (what), ¿quién? (who), ¿dónde? (where), ¿cuándo? (when), ¿por qué? (why), ¿cómo? (how).
Negatives: put "no" before the verb. "Nunca" means never.
"Porque" (one word, no accent) means "because".
lessons.try: Interview a partner with six question words.

learn: -er: -o, -es, -e, -emos, -éis, -en (comer: como, comes, come...).
-ir: -o, -es, -e, -imos, -ís, -en (vivir: vivo, vives, vive...).
Only the nosotros and vosotros forms differ.
lessons.try: Conjugate beber and escribir.

learn: Las matemáticas, la biología, la historia, el inglés, el arte, la informática (computing).
Opinions: fácil (easy), difícil, interesante, aburrido, útil (useful).
"La biología es interesante pero difícil."
lessons.try: Give your opinion of five subjects.

learn: "Tengo historia a las diez."
"Primero... luego... después... por fin" (first, then, after, finally).
"El horario" is a timetable.
lessons.try: Describe your school day using sequence words.

learn: Gustar means "to be pleasing to": "Me gusta el fútbol" literally means "Football is pleasing to me."
Use "gusta" with one thing or an infinitive; "gustan" with plural things.
Pronouns: me, te, le, nos, les.
check: "Me gustan los perros" uses gustan because perros is...
lessons.try: Write five things you like and three you don't.

learn: Jugar al fútbol, montar en bicicleta, ir al cine, leer, pasear, jugar videojuegos.
"En mi tiempo libre..." means "In my free time..."
"¿Qué te gusta hacer?" asks "What do you like to do?"
lessons.try: Survey classmates on their favourite free-time activity.

learn: "Me encanta" means "I love" (it delights me).
"A mí también" means "Me too"; "A mí tampoco" means "Me neither."
Use "a mí", "a ti" for emphasis.
lessons.try: Have a conversation agreeing and disagreeing about hobbies.

learn: Estar: estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis, están.
Use estar for location (Estoy en casa) and temporary states (Estoy cansado).
"¿Cómo estás?" uses estar because feelings change.
lessons.try: Say where you are and how you feel at five times of day.

learn: El hospital, la farmacia, el supermercado, el banco, la estación de tren, el ayuntamiento (town hall).
Directions: a la derecha (to the right), a la izquierda (left), todo recto (straight ahead).
"¿Dónde está la farmacia?" "Está al lado del banco."
lessons.try: Give directions from school to your home in Spanish.

learn: Ser for permanent things: identity, origin, characteristics, time.
Estar for location and conditions.
Meaning can change: "Es listo" (he's clever) / "Está listo" (he's ready).
lessons.try: Write ten sentences choosing ser or estar.

units.t: Ir, Ir a + Infinitive and Tener

learn: Ir: voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van.
a + el = al: "Voy al parque."
"Vamos" can also mean "Let's go!"
lessons.try: Describe where you go each day.

learn: Ir a + infinitive: "Voy a estudiar" (I'm going to study).
Time expressions: esta tarde, mañana, la próxima semana (next week).
"¿Qué vas a hacer el sábado?"
lessons.try: Plan your weekend in Spanish.

learn: Tener: tengo, tienes, tiene, tenemos, tenéis, tienen.
Tener años (age), tener hambre, tener sed, tener frío, tener calor, tener prisa (be in a hurry).
Tener que + infinitive (have to).
lessons.try: Write about your obligations using tener que.

learn: e → ie: querer (quiero), pensar (pienso), empezar (empiezo).
o → ue: poder (puedo), dormir (duermo), volver (vuelvo). u → ue: jugar (juego).
e → i: pedir (pido), servir (sirvo). Nosotros forms don't change.
lessons.try: Write sentences with one verb from each group.

learn: Padres, hermanos, abuelos, tíos, primos, sobrinos (nephews/nieces), nietos (grandchildren).
Possessives: mi/mis, tu/tus, su/sus, nuestro/nuestra.
"Nuestra familia es grande."
lessons.try: Describe your family tree in Spanish.

learn: Extended families often live close together and gather for meals in many Spanish-speaking countries.
Sunday lunch is a major family event in Spain.
Many people have two surnames: their father's and their mother's.
lessons.try: Write your full name the Spanish way, with both surnames.
